question: Perform Factor Analysis on a behavioral or survey dataset to identify underlying latent traits (e.g., anxiety, depression). Use parallel analysis (100 iterations, 95th percentile, random_state=42) to select the number of factors. Report factor loadings.

files.eval_guideline: Each survey item's factor loading values must match the reference within +/-0.05; sign of each factor may be flipped, column order and item label formatting may differ.
files.match_reasoning: The filenames are identical and both files are CSVs holding the factor loadings table.

parameters.question: Compare factor loading tables from Factor Analysis (number of factors chosen by parallel analysis, 100 iterations, 95th percentile, random_state=42). Each survey item's loading on each factor must match the reference within +/-0.05. The sign of a whole factor may be flipped, factor column order may differ, and item label formatting may differ (e.g., case or prefixes). Match items by row label and factors by best-matching loading pattern (allowing sign flip) before comparing values.

files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline asks for record-level matching of each item's loadings within ±0.05. Factor sign flips, column order and label formatting are allowed to differ, and approximate alignment handles all of these. Parallel analysis uses a fixed seed, so the results are deterministic within that tolerance and a value-by-value table comparison works better than summary.

align_plan.reasoning: Both tables have the same layout: one row per survey item and one column per factor, so no transpose is needed. The column names match exactly, so each column is mapped to the column of the same name. Rows are matched on the 'Item' label, the stable identifier for each survey item. Loadings are computed values, so they are not used as keys. Row order doesn't matter (it's a set of items), so the rows are sorted by Item and checked as a permutation. Per the guideline, factor signs and column order may differ. The reference loadings look unrotated (Factor_1 has a large negative loading on every item), while the candidate's look rotated (each group of items loads on its own factor). That means the factor columns may not match up one-to-one by name, so sign-flipping or reordering factors needs to happen at the value-comparison stage. A fixed name-based mapping can't fix that.

comparison_plan.overall_reasoning:
The rows are factor loadings for 20 survey items, aligned on Item. All three factor columns matter equally, because the guideline says every item's loading must match the reference within ±0.05.

How the guideline maps onto the available strategies:
- **Strategy:** each column uses cell-by-cell RAE.
- **Sign:** compare_abs is set to true because the guideline allows a factor's sign to flip. Factor signs in factor analysis are arbitrary. One limitation: this ignores sign per cell, not per whole factor, so it is a little more lenient than the guideline.
- **Tolerance:** RAE measures relative error, so the absolute ±0.05 band can't be set directly. Most loadings are roughly 0.25–0.8 in size, and 0.05 relative to a loading of about 0.35 is about 0.15, so I used a tolerance of 0.15. Loadings near zero will be judged more strictly than the guideline intends.
- **Column order:** the guideline allows factors to come in a different order, but the plan can't reorder columns, so they are matched by name.

Note on the data: the reference loadings look unrotated. Factor 1 is negative for every item at about -0.3, which is typical of a general first factor. The candidate's loadings look rotated (e.g., varimax), with items 1–6 at about 0.75 on Factor_1 and items 7–10 at about 0.78 on Factor_2. The two solutions differ a lot, and most cells will fail even with the sign ignored. That reflects a real methodological difference, not a problem with the comparison setup.
